paragraphs.title: An Invitation to Praise the Lord as Creator and Redeemer

answers: Sing and make a joyful noise unto the Lord
Go to war
Build a city
easy.explanation: The psalmist calls the people to sing and make a joyful noise unto the Lord.
easy.q: What does the psalmist invite the people to do?

answers: The king of the earth
The rock of our salvation
The shepherd of the wilderness
easy.explanation: The verse calls the Lord “the rock of our salvation.”
easy.q: How is the Lord described in verse 1?

answers: Only the mountains
Only the sea
The sea and the dry land
easy.explanation: The verse says, “The sea is his,” and that His hands formed the dry land.
easy.q: What belongs to the Lord according to verse 5?

answers: Singing, making a joyful noise, and giving thanks
Keeping silent, fasting, and sleeping
Walking, fighting, and fleeing
medium.explanation: The people are called to sing, make a joyful noise, and come before the Lord with thanksgiving.
medium.q: What sequence of actions is encouraged at the beginning of the passage?

answers: The paths through the hills
The power or heights of the mountains
The rivers in the hills
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the hills and their great strength or heights, which belong to the Lord.
medium.q: What does the phrase “the strength of the hills” refer to?

answers: He rules only over mankind
He is king only over the land
The earth and sea belong to Him and were made by Him
medium.explanation: The Lord is great because all creation belongs to Him and was formed by His hands.
medium.q: How do these verses explain the greatness of the Lord?

answers: It presents Him as the source of salvation, worthy of praise
It shows that He hides Himself from the people
It suggests that He needs salvation from the people
challenge.explanation: The title presents the Lord as the dependable source of salvation, so He is worthy of praise.
challenge.q: How does the title “the rock of our salvation” support the call to praise the Lord?

answers: Because they are merely distant places
Because all the realms of creation belong to Him
Because the mountains are stronger than He is
challenge.explanation: The passage shows that every part of creation is under the Lord’s authority and was made by Him.
challenge.q: Why do the sea, dry land, depths, and hills strengthen the description of the Lord as a great King?

answers: The passage moves from a call to praise to reasons for the Lord’s greatness
The passage moves from war to peace
The passage moves from describing the people to describing their enemies
challenge.explanation: The first verses call the people to worship, while the later verses explain why the Lord deserves that worship.
challenge.q: What change of emphasis takes place between verses 1–2 and verses 3–5?

paragraphs.title: Worship and Reliance on the Lord’s Guidance

answers: Worship, bow down, and kneel
Run, leap, and shout
Sit, sleep, and remain silent
easy.explanation: Verse 6 says, “O come, let us worship and bow down: let us kneel before the LORD our maker.”
easy.q: What actions does the psalmist call the people to perform before the Lord?

answers: As the kings of the earth
As the people of His pasture and the sheep of His hand
As the army of the mountains
easy.explanation: The verse describes them as “the people of his pasture” and “the sheep of his hand.”

answers: To bring water
To conquer the land
To hear the Lord’s voice
easy.explanation: The verse says, “To day if ye will hear his voice.”
easy.q: What is required according to the end of verse 7?

answers: People whom the Lord shepherds and cares for
People who live on a high mountain
People who serve in a great temple
medium.explanation: The pasture image presents the Lord as the shepherd who cares for and guides His people.
medium.q: What does the phrase “the people of his pasture” suggest?

answers: Bowing shows honor to the One who made them
Bowing hides the people from the Lord
Bowing replaces hearing His voice
medium.explanation: The people bow because the Lord is their maker and therefore deserves their honor.
medium.q: What is the relationship between bowing before the Lord and calling Him “our maker”?

answers: Hearing His voice
Being stronger than He is
Moving far away from Him
medium.explanation: The passage connects belonging to the Lord with hearing His voice.
medium.q: What condition is connected with following the Lord’s guidance?

answers: The people are completely independent and need no guidance
The Lord guides and protects His people
The people rule over all creation
challenge.explanation: The sheep image presents the Lord as the guide and protector of His people.
challenge.q: What does the image of Israel as sheep teach about the relationship between the Lord and His people?

answers: It shows that worship includes listening and obeying
It removes the need for worship
It refers only to the creation of the sea
challenge.explanation: The passage joins outward worship with a willing response to the Lord’s voice.
challenge.q: How does the phrase “To day if ye will hear his voice” connect with the call to worship?

answers: The Lord made His people and continues to hold and guide them
The people made the Lord and guide Him
The Lord belongs only to the land and not to the people
challenge.explanation: The expressions show that the Lord is both the Creator and the continuing guide of His people.
challenge.q: What shared truth is expressed by “our maker” and “the sheep of his hand”?

paragraphs.title: A Warning against Hardening the Heart and Its Consequences

answers: Harden their hearts
Sing too much
Walk in the wilderness
easy.explanation: The warning is, “Harden not your heart.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist warn the people not to do?

answers: Jerusalem and Hebron
The provocation and the day of temptation in the wilderness
The sea and the dry land
easy.explanation: The passage recalls the provocation and the day of temptation in the wilderness.
easy.q: Which places are remembered as the setting where the people tested the Lord?

answers: The generation would enter His rest
The generation would not enter His rest
The generation would rule over the hills
easy.explanation: The Lord swore that they should not enter His rest.
easy.q: What was the result of the Lord’s oath?

answers: To sing
To go astray
To bless
medium.explanation: To err means to go astray or wander from the right way.
medium.q: In the phrase “a people that do err in their heart,” what does “err” mean?

answers: They did not build a temple
They went astray in their hearts and did not know His ways
They did not recognize the sea
medium.explanation: The passage says they were a people who went astray in their hearts and did not know the Lord’s ways.
medium.q: Why was the Lord grieved with that generation?

answers: They tempted and proved the Lord
They sang thanksgiving psalms
They bowed before the hills
medium.explanation: The verse says, “When your fathers tempted me, proved me, and saw my work.”
medium.q: What did the fathers do in the wilderness?

answers: Hearing the Lord’s voice causes the heart to go astray
Hardening and wandering of the heart lead to exclusion from the Lord’s rest
Seeing the Lord’s works always guarantees entrance into His rest
challenge.explanation: The people tested the Lord, went astray in their hearts, and consequently were denied entrance into His rest.
challenge.q: What is the central cause-and-effect relationship in this passage?

answers: They tested the Lord even though they had seen His works
They had never heard of the Lord’s works
They saw only the hills and not the Lord
challenge.explanation: The phrase highlights that their testing of the Lord occurred despite witnessing His works.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “and saw my work” emphasize about the people’s sin?

answers: The Promised Land
The sea
The wilderness
challenge.explanation: In the context of Israel’s wilderness journey, the Lord’s rest represents entry into the Promised Land.
challenge.q: What does “my rest” most likely represent in the context of the passage?
